Plot separable treatment effects

Source: R/plot.R
plot.biscal_aste.Rd

Plots the estimated effects with Wald confidence intervals. When the effects were computed at several end time points (a vector K in aste() or easte()), they are drawn as curves over the end time with pointwise confidence bands; otherwise as points with interval bars.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'biscal_aste'
plot(
  x,
  effects = c("STE1", "STE2", "TTE"),
  profiles = NULL,
  band = TRUE,
  col = NULL,
  main = NULL,
  xlab = "End time K",
  ylab = "Effect (log GOR ratio)",
  ylim = NULL,
  legend = TRUE,
  mfrow = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'biscal_easte'
plot(
  x,
  effects = c("ESTE1", "ESTE2", "ETTE"),
  band = TRUE,
  col = NULL,
  main = "",
  xlab = "End time K",
  ylab = "Average effect (log GOR ratio)",
  ylim = NULL,
  legend = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A result of aste() or easte().

effects

Effects to draw. For aste() results any of "STE1", "STE2", "TTE", "ASTE1", "ASTE2" and "DASTE"; for easte() results any of "ESTE1", "ESTE2", "ETTE", "EASTE1", "EASTE2" and "DEASTE".

profiles

For aste() results, the covariate profiles (row numbers of newdata) to draw, one panel each.

band

Draw confidence intervals?

col

Colors, one per effect.

main

Panel titles; by default the covariate values of each profile.

xlab, ylab

Axis labels.

ylim

Vertical range; by default it covers the intervals and zero.

legend

Draw a legend (for curves over the end time)?

mfrow

Panel layout c(rows, columns) for several profiles.

...

Further graphical arguments passed to graphics::plot().

Value

NULL, invisibly. Called for its side effect.

Examples

fit <- biscal(cbind(y1, y2) ~ x1 + x2, data = simtrial, id = "id",
              time = "visit", treatment = "trt")
res <- aste(fit, newdata = data.frame(x1 = 0, x2 = 1), K = 1:10)
plot(res)

plot(res, effects = "DASTE")
